Carmack speaking about "The Dawn of Mobile VR" during the [Game Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Conference "Game Developers Conference") 2015

In February 2017, Carmack sued ZeniMax, claiming the company had refused to pay him the remaining $22.5 million (~$28.2 million in 2024) owed to him from their purchase of id Software.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-28) In October 2018, Carmack stated that he and ZeniMax had reached an agreement and that "Zenimax has fully satisfied their obligations to me", ending the suit.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-29)

On November 13, 2019, Carmack stepped down from the Oculus CTO role to become a "Consulting CTO" in order to allocate more time to his work on [artificial general intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence") (AGI).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-consultant-4) On August 19, 2022, Carmack announced that he has raised $20M for Keen Technologies, his new AGI company.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-keenagi-30) On December 16, 2022, Carmack left Oculus to focus on Keen.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-:0-7)

In September 2023 John partnered with [reinforcement learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforcement_learning "Reinforcement learning") researcher [Richard S. Sutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_S._Sutton "Richard S. Sutton"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-31) though Sutton left in 2026 to launch the AI startup Oak Lab.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-32)

### Workstyle

Carmack claims to have maintained a sixty-hour work week, working a 10-hour day, six days a week, throughout his career.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33) He has spoken publicly about the importance of long hours of uninterrupted focus in his work. Not only does high intensity allow him to make progress more quickly, but long hours are also critical to maintaining a focused mindset over time. Despite working such a demanding schedule, he has never experienced burnout.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33)

Carmack is also known for taking week-long programming retreats. These retreats involve a solitary, uninterrupted period away from his normal routine often sequestered in a random city and hotel.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner2003252-34) The goal of these retreats is to allow Carmack to operate at full cognitive capacity, tackling a specific, difficult problem or learning a new skill.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-35) The solitude and physical isolation of these retreats offer an environment for deep focus and reflection, making them an essential part of Carmack's creative process.

Carmack was vocal about his frustration with the bureaucratic inefficiencies he encountered during his time at Meta.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-36) In his departure memo, he stated, "We have a ridiculous amount of people and resources, but we constantly self-sabotage and squander effort," he wrote. "I have never been able to kill stupid things before they cause damage, or set a direction and have a team actually stick to it."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-37)

Carmack subscribes to the philosophy that small, incremental steps are the fastest route to meaningful and [disruptive innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptive_innovation "Disruptive innovation").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33) He compares this approach to the "magic of [gradient descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent "Gradient descent")" where small steps using local information result in the best outcomes. According to Carmack, this principle is proven by his own experience, and he has observed this in many of the smartest people in the world. He states, "Little tiny steps using local information winds up leading to all the best answers."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33)

## Armadillo Aerospace

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo%2C_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9%2C_2005.jpg/250px-John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo%2C_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9%2C_2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo,_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9,_2005.jpg)

Carmack during the 2005 [X PRIZE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansari_X_PRIZE "Ansari X PRIZE") Cup

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg/250px-John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg)

Carmack in 2008

Around 2000, Carmack became interested in rocketry, a hobby of his youth. He began by giving financial support to a few local amateur engineers. Carmack funded the company [Armadillo Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo_Aerospace "Armadillo Aerospace") out of his own pocket, for "something north of a million dollars a year."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-nsj20130801-38) The company of hobbyists made steady progress toward their goals of suborbital space flight and eventual orbital vehicles. In October 2008, Armadillo Aerospace competed in a NASA contest known as the [Lunar Lander Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Lander_Challenge "Lunar Lander Challenge"), winning first place in the Level 1 competition along with $350,000 (~$499,182 in 2024).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-39) In September 2009, they completed Level 2 and were awarded $500,000 (~$708,446 in 2024).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-d0-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Armadillo_Aerospace_Claim_Level_2_NGLLC_Prize-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Lunar_lander_qualifies_for_prize-42) The company went into "hibernation mode" in 2013.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-nsj20130801-38)

According to Carmack, the work in the aerospace industry is "simple" compared to the work he does in video games.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-43)

## Open-source software

Carmack is an advocate of [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software"), and has repeatedly voiced his opposition to [software patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent "Software patent"), equating them to robbery.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-44) He has also contributed to open-source projects, such as starting the initial port of the [X Window System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Window_System "X Window System") to [Mac OS X Server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_OS_X_Server "Mac OS X Server") and working to improve the OpenGL drivers for Linux through the [Utah GLX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_GLX "Utah GLX") project.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-45)

Carmack released the source code for _Wolfenstein 3D_ in 1995 and the _Doom_ source code in 1997, first under a custom license and then under the [GNU General Public License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License "GNU General Public License") (GPL) in 1999. When the source code to _Quake_ was leaked and circulated among the _Quake_ community underground in 1997 after licensee Crack dot Com was hacked,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-46) a programmer unaffiliated with id Software named Greg Alexander used it to [port _Quake_ to Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_Quake_port "Linux Quake port") using [SVGALib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SVGALib "SVGALib"). As this was more feature rich than [Dave Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Taylor_(game_programmer) "Dave Taylor (game programmer)")'s earlier [X11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X11 "X11") port, he sent the patches to Carmack.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-47) Instead of pursuing legal action, id Software used the patches as the foundation for a company-sanctioned [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux") port maintained by new hire Zoid Kirsch, who later ported _Quakeworld_ and _Quake II_ to Linux as well.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-48)

id Software has since publicly released the source code to _Quake_ in 1999, _Quake 2_ in 2001, _Quake 3_ in 2005 and lastly _Doom 3_ in 2011 (and later the _BFG Edition_ in 2012). The source code for _[Hovertank 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hovertank\_3D "Hovertank 3D")_ and _[Catacomb 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catacomb\_3D "Catacomb 3D")_ (as well as Carmack's earlier _[Catacomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catacomb\_(video\_game) "Catacomb (video game)")_) was released in June 2014 by [Flat Rock Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flat_Rock_Software "Flat Rock Software") with Carmack's blessing.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-50) He has since expressed regret on using the [copyleft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyleft "Copyleft") GPL over the more [permissive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permissive_license "Permissive license")[BSD license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BSD_license "BSD license").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-51)

The release of [id Tech 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Tech_4 "Id Tech 4") occurred despite patent concerns from [Creative Labs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Labs "Creative Labs") over [Carmack's reverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmack's_reverse "Carmack's reverse"),[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-52) while the original _Doom_ source release shipped without music due to complications with the [Cygnus Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cygnus_Studios "Cygnus Studios") developed DMX library (which led to the [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux")[version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Doom_ports#Linux "List of Doom ports") being selected for release).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-53) Carmack has since advised developers to be careful when utilizing middleware, noting how it can limit the possibilities of later releasing source code.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-54)[Tim Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Sweeney_(game_developer) "Tim Sweeney (game developer)") has implied this issue has hindered potential releases of older [Unreal Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Engine "Unreal Engine") source code.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-55)

On the other hand, despite his technical admiration for the system,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-56) Carmack has several times over the years voiced a skeptical opinion about [Linux as a gaming platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_as_a_gaming_platform "Linux as a gaming platform").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-58) In 2013, he argued for [emulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emulation_(computing) "Emulation (computing)") as the "proper technical direction for gaming on Linux",[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-59) and in 2014 he voiced the opinion that Linux might be the biggest problem for the success of the [Steam Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_Machines "Steam Machines").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-60)

Carmack contributes to charities and gaming communities. Some of the recipients of Carmack's [charitable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charitable_organization "Charitable organization") contributions include his former high school, promoters of open-source software, opponents of software patents, and game enthusiasts.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-61)

## Personal life

Carmack was so successful at id that by mid-1994 he had purchased two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferraris "Ferraris"): a [Ferrari 328](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_328 "Ferrari 328") and a [Ferrari Testarossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_Testarossa "Ferrari Testarossa").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-lombardi199407-62) In 1997, he gave away the Ferrari 328 as a prize to [Dennis Fong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Fong "Dennis Fong"), the winner of the _Quake_ tournament "[Red Annihilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Annihilation "Red Annihilation")".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-63)

He met his now ex-wife [Katherine Anna Kang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Anna_Kang "Katherine Anna Kang") at the 1997 [QuakeCon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuakeCon "QuakeCon") when she visited id's offices. As a bet, Kang challenged Carmack to sponsor the first all-female _Quake_ tournament if she was able to produce a significant number of participants. Carmack predicted a maximum of 25 participants, but there were 1,500.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner2003281-64) Carmack and Kang married on January 1, 2000, and planned a ceremony in Hawaii. Steve Jobs requested that they would postpone the ceremony so Carmack could attend the MacWorld Expo on January 5, 2000. Carmack declined and suggested making a video instead.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-65) Carmack and Kang had a son Christopher Ryan in August 2004.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-66) Their second son was born in November 2009.

Carmack is divorced as of 2021. On May 26, 2022, he announced his divorce and how he met his partner Trista through the VR _[Beat Saber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat\_Saber "Beat Saber")_ games he would host via Twitter.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-67)

As a game developer, Carmack differed from many of his contemporaries by avoiding commitment to a final release date for any game he was developing. Instead, when asked for a release date on a new game, Carmack would usually reply that the game would be released "when it's done".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-68) Employees at [Apogee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_Realms "3D Realms"), in their past years the publishers of games by id Software, adopted this business practice as well.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-69) In 2019, as a guest on _[The Joe Rogan Experience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Joe\_Rogan\_Experience "The Joe Rogan Experience")_, Carmack stated that his beliefs have changed over time: "I largely recant from that now." On _[Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage\_(video\_game) "Rage (video game)")_'s six-year development time he says: "I think we should have done whatever it would have taken to ship that two years earlier." Carmack also reflected on the internal development of Quake in this regard and described it as "traumatic" and says id Software could have split the game into two parts and shipped it earlier.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-70)

Carmack has a [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog "Blog") last updated in 2006 (previously a [.plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger_protocol "Finger protocol") on id Software's server, under the username `johnc`[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-71)), an active [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account, and also occasionally posts comments to _[Slashdot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slashdot "Slashdot")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-slashdot-answers-10)

Carmack supported the [2012 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul_2012_presidential_campaign "Ron Paul 2012 presidential campaign") of [Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)")[Ron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul "Ron Paul"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-72) and also persuaded the [Libertarian Party of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_of_Texas "Libertarian Party of Texas") to accept [bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin "Bitcoin") as an alternative to donations.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-73) He is an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheism "Atheism").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-75) During a conversation with [Joe Rogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Rogan "Joe Rogan"), Carmack revealed that he had trained in Brazilian Jiu Jitsu and [Judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") for several years as a hobby.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-76)

During his time at id Software, a medium pepperoni pizza would arrive for Carmack from [Domino's Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domino's_Pizza "Domino's Pizza") almost every day,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-77) carried by the same delivery person for more than 15 years. Carmack had been such a regular customer that they continued to charge him 1995 prices.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-78)

On occasion he has commended the efforts of similarly focused programmers– first [Ken Silverman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Silverman "Ken Silverman"), who wrote the [Build engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build_(game_engine) "Build (game engine)") for [3D Realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_Realms "3D Realms"), and later with [Tim Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Sweeney_(game_developer) "Tim Sweeney (game developer)") of [Epic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Games "Epic Games"), who wrote the [Unreal Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Engine "Unreal Engine").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-slashdot-answers-10)

**John D. Carmack II**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-wired.com-2) (born August 21,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-dob-1) 1970)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-wired.com-2) is an American [computer programmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programmer "Computer programmer") and [video game developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_developer "Video game developer"). He co-founded the video game company [id Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Software "Id Software") and was the lead programmer of its 1990s games _[Commander Keen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander\_Keen "Commander Keen")_, _[Wolfenstein 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfenstein\_3D "Wolfenstein 3D")_, _[Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doom\_(1993\_video\_game) "Doom (1993 video game)")_, _[Quake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quake\_(video\_game) "Quake (video game)")_, and their sequels. Carmack made innovations in [3D computer graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics"), such as his Carmack's Reverse algorithm for [shadow volumes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadow_volume "Shadow volume").

In 2013, he resigned from id Software to work full-time at [Oculus VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_Labs "Reality Labs") as their [CTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_technology_officer "Chief technology officer"). In 2019, he reduced his role to Consulting CTO so he could allocate more time toward [artificial general intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence") (AGI).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-consultant-4) In 2022, he left Oculus to work on his AGI startup, Keen Technologies.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-:0-7)

## Biography

### Early life

Carmack was born in [Shawnee Mission, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawnee_Mission,_Kansas "Shawnee Mission, Kansas"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-wired.com-2) the son of local television news reporter Stan Carmack. He grew up in the [Kansas City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"), where he became interested in [computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer "Computer") at an early age. He attended [Shawnee Mission East High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawnee_Mission_East_High_School "Shawnee Mission East High School") in [Prairie Village, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie_Village,_Kansas "Prairie Village, Kansas") and [Raytown South High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raytown_South_High_School "Raytown South High School") in nearby [Raytown, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raytown,_Missouri "Raytown, Missouri").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner200320%E2%80%9322-8)

Carmack was introduced to video games with the 1978 [shoot 'em up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot_'em_up "Shoot 'em up") game _[Space Invaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Invaders "Space Invaders")_ in the [arcades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_game "Arcade game") during a [summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer "Summer") vacation as a child. The 1980 [maze chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maze_game "Maze game") arcade game _[Pac-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-Man "Pac-Man")_ also left a strong impression on him. He cited [Nintendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo "Nintendo") designer [Shigeru Miyamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeru_Miyamoto "Shigeru Miyamoto") as the game developer he most admired.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-9)

As reported in David Kushner's _[Masters of Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters\_of\_Doom "Masters of Doom")_, when Carmack was 14, he broke into a school with other children to steal [Apple II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_II "Apple II") computers. To gain entry to the building, Carmack concocted a sticky substance of [thermite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermite "Thermite") mixed with [Vaseline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaseline "Vaseline") that melted through the windows. However, an overweight accomplice struggled to get through the hole and instead opened the window, setting off a silent alarm and alerting police. Carmack was arrested and sent for psychiatric evaluation. He was sentenced to a year in a juvenile home.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-slashdot-answers-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner200321-11) He attended the [University of Missouri–Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Missouri%E2%80%93Kansas_City "University of Missouri–Kansas City") for two semesters before withdrawing to work as a freelance programmer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-12)

### Career

[Softdisk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softdisk "Softdisk"), a computer company in [Shreveport, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreveport,_Louisiana "Shreveport, Louisiana"), hired Carmack to work on _[Softdisk G-S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softdisk\_(disk\_magazine) "Softdisk (disk magazine)")_ (an [Apple II GS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_IIGS "Apple IIGS") publication), introducing him to [John Romero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Romero "John Romero") and other future key members of id Software such as [Adrian Carmack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Carmack "Adrian Carmack") (no relation). Later, Softdisk would place this team in charge of a new, but short-lived, bi-monthly game subscription product called _Gamer's Edge_ for the IBM PC (DOS) platform. In 1990, while still at Softdisk, Carmack, Romero, and others created the first of the _[Commander Keen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander\_Keen "Commander Keen")_ games, a series that was published by [Apogee Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apogee_Software "Apogee Software"), under the [shareware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shareware "Shareware") distribution model, from 1991 onwards.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner200363%E2%80%9366-13) Afterwards, Carmack left Softdisk to co-found [id Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Software "Id Software").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner200374-14)

Carmack has pioneered or popularized the use of many techniques in computer graphics, including "[adaptive tile refresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptive_tile_refresh "Adaptive tile refresh")" for _Commander Keen_,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner200350-15)[ray casting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_casting "Ray casting") for _[Hovertank 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hovertank\_3D "Hovertank 3D")_, _[Catacomb 3-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catacomb\_3-D "Catacomb 3-D")_, and _Wolfenstein 3D_, [binary space partitioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_space_partitioning "Binary space partitioning") which _Doom_ became the first game to use,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner2003142-16)[surface caching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_caching "Surface caching") which he invented for _Quake_, [Carmack's Reverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmack's_Reverse "Carmack's Reverse") (formally known as z-fail stencil shadows) which he devised for _Doom 3_, and [MegaTexture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MegaTexture "MegaTexture") technology, first used in _[Enemy Territory: Quake Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enemy\_Territory:\_Quake\_Wars "Enemy Territory: Quake Wars")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-17)_[Quake 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quake\_3 "Quake 3")_ popularized the [fast inverse square root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_inverse_square_root "Fast inverse square root") algorithm.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-18)

Carmack's engines have also been licensed for use in other influential first-person shooters such as _[Half-Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-Life\_(video\_game) "Half-Life (video game)")_, _[Call of Duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty\_(video\_game) "Call of Duty (video game)")_ and _[Medal of Honor: Allied Assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal\_of\_Honor:\_Allied\_Assault "Medal of Honor: Allied Assault")_. In 2005, Carmack developed his first game for mobile phones, [Doom RPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doom_RPG "Doom RPG").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-20)

On August 7, 2013, Carmack joined [Oculus VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oculus_VR "Oculus VR") as their [CTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_technology_officer "Chief technology officer").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-21) On November 22, 2013, he resigned from [id Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Software "Id Software") to work full-time at Oculus VR.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-polygon-3)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-22) Carmack's reason for leaving was that id's parent company [ZeniMax Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZeniMax_Media "ZeniMax Media") did not want to support Oculus Rift.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-23) Carmack's role at both companies later became central to [a ZeniMax lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZeniMax_v._Oculus "ZeniMax v. Oculus") against Oculus' parent company, [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") (then known as Facebook), claiming that Oculus stole ZeniMax's virtual reality [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property "Intellectual property").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-26) The trial jury absolved Carmack of liability, though Oculus and other corporate officers were held liable for trademark, copyright, and contract violations.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-27)

In February 2017, Carmack sued ZeniMax, claiming the company had refused to pay him the remaining $22.5 million (~$28.2 million in 2024) owed to him from their purchase of id Software.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-28) In October 2018, Carmack stated that he and ZeniMax had reached an agreement and that "Zenimax has fully satisfied their obligations to me", ending the suit.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-29)

On November 13, 2019, Carmack stepped down from the Oculus CTO role to become a "Consulting CTO" in order to allocate more time to his work on [artificial general intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence") (AGI).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-consultant-4) On August 19, 2022, Carmack announced that he has raised $20M for Keen Technologies, his new AGI company.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-keenagi-30) On December 16, 2022, Carmack left Oculus to focus on Keen.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-:0-7)

In September 2023 John partnered with [reinforcement learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforcement_learning "Reinforcement learning") researcher [Richard S. Sutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_S._Sutton "Richard S. Sutton"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-31) though Sutton left in 2026 to launch the AI startup Oak Lab.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-32)

### Workstyle

Carmack claims to have maintained a sixty-hour work week, working a 10-hour day, six days a week, throughout his career.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33) He has spoken publicly about the importance of long hours of uninterrupted focus in his work. Not only does high intensity allow him to make progress more quickly, but long hours are also critical to maintaining a focused mindset over time. Despite working such a demanding schedule, he has never experienced burnout.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33)

Carmack is also known for taking week-long programming retreats. These retreats involve a solitary, uninterrupted period away from his normal routine often sequestered in a random city and hotel.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner2003252-34) The goal of these retreats is to allow Carmack to operate at full cognitive capacity, tackling a specific, difficult problem or learning a new skill.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-35) The solitude and physical isolation of these retreats offer an environment for deep focus and reflection, making them an essential part of Carmack's creative process.

Carmack was vocal about his frustration with the bureaucratic inefficiencies he encountered during his time at Meta.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-36) In his departure memo, he stated, "We have a ridiculous amount of people and resources, but we constantly self-sabotage and squander effort," he wrote. "I have never been able to kill stupid things before they cause damage, or set a direction and have a team actually stick to it."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-37)

Carmack subscribes to the philosophy that small, incremental steps are the fastest route to meaningful and [disruptive innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptive_innovation "Disruptive innovation").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33) He compares this approach to the "magic of [gradient descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent "Gradient descent")" where small steps using local information result in the best outcomes. According to Carmack, this principle is proven by his own experience, and he has observed this in many of the smartest people in the world. He states, "Little tiny steps using local information winds up leading to all the best answers."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Fridman-33)

## Armadillo Aerospace

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo%2C_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9%2C_2005.jpg/250px-John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo%2C_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9%2C_2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Carmack_during_the_X-Prize_Cup_2005_in_Las_Cruces_and_Alamogordo,_New_Mexico_--_October_6-9,_2005.jpg)

Carmack during the 2005 [X PRIZE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansari_X_PRIZE "Ansari X PRIZE") Cup

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg/250px-John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John-carmack-by-bill-cramer.jpg)

Carmack in 2008

Around 2000, Carmack became interested in rocketry, a hobby of his youth. He began by giving financial support to a few local amateur engineers. Carmack funded the company [Armadillo Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo_Aerospace "Armadillo Aerospace") out of his own pocket, for "something north of a million dollars a year."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-nsj20130801-38) The company of hobbyists made steady progress toward their goals of suborbital space flight and eventual orbital vehicles. In October 2008, Armadillo Aerospace competed in a NASA contest known as the [Lunar Lander Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Lander_Challenge "Lunar Lander Challenge"), winning first place in the Level 1 competition along with $350,000 (~$499,182 in 2024).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-39) In September 2009, they completed Level 2 and were awarded $500,000 (~$708,446 in 2024).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-d0-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Armadillo_Aerospace_Claim_Level_2_NGLLC_Prize-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-Lunar_lander_qualifies_for_prize-42) The company went into "hibernation mode" in 2013.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-nsj20130801-38)

According to Carmack, the work in the aerospace industry is "simple" compared to the work he does in video games.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-43)

## Open-source software

Carmack is an advocate of [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software"), and has repeatedly voiced his opposition to [software patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_patent "Software patent"), equating them to robbery.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-44) He has also contributed to open-source projects, such as starting the initial port of the [X Window System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Window_System "X Window System") to [Mac OS X Server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_OS_X_Server "Mac OS X Server") and working to improve the OpenGL drivers for Linux through the [Utah GLX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_GLX "Utah GLX") project.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-45)

Carmack released the source code for _Wolfenstein 3D_ in 1995 and the _Doom_ source code in 1997, first under a custom license and then under the [GNU General Public License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License "GNU General Public License") (GPL) in 1999. When the source code to _Quake_ was leaked and circulated among the _Quake_ community underground in 1997 after licensee Crack dot Com was hacked,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-46) a programmer unaffiliated with id Software named Greg Alexander used it to [port _Quake_ to Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_Quake_port "Linux Quake port") using [SVGALib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SVGALib "SVGALib"). As this was more feature rich than [Dave Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Taylor_(game_programmer) "Dave Taylor (game programmer)")'s earlier [X11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X11 "X11") port, he sent the patches to Carmack.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-47) Instead of pursuing legal action, id Software used the patches as the foundation for a company-sanctioned [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux") port maintained by new hire Zoid Kirsch, who later ported _Quakeworld_ and _Quake II_ to Linux as well.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-48)

id Software has since publicly released the source code to _Quake_ in 1999, _Quake 2_ in 2001, _Quake 3_ in 2005 and lastly _Doom 3_ in 2011 (and later the _BFG Edition_ in 2012). The source code for _[Hovertank 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hovertank\_3D "Hovertank 3D")_ and _[Catacomb 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catacomb\_3D "Catacomb 3D")_ (as well as Carmack's earlier _[Catacomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catacomb\_(video\_game) "Catacomb (video game)")_) was released in June 2014 by [Flat Rock Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flat_Rock_Software "Flat Rock Software") with Carmack's blessing.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-50) He has since expressed regret on using the [copyleft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyleft "Copyleft") GPL over the more [permissive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permissive_license "Permissive license")[BSD license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BSD_license "BSD license").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-51)

The release of [id Tech 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Tech_4 "Id Tech 4") occurred despite patent concerns from [Creative Labs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Labs "Creative Labs") over [Carmack's reverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmack's_reverse "Carmack's reverse"),[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-52) while the original _Doom_ source release shipped without music due to complications with the [Cygnus Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cygnus_Studios "Cygnus Studios") developed DMX library (which led to the [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux")[version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Doom_ports#Linux "List of Doom ports") being selected for release).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-53) Carmack has since advised developers to be careful when utilizing middleware, noting how it can limit the possibilities of later releasing source code.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-54)[Tim Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Sweeney_(game_developer) "Tim Sweeney (game developer)") has implied this issue has hindered potential releases of older [Unreal Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Engine "Unreal Engine") source code.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-55)

On the other hand, despite his technical admiration for the system,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-56) Carmack has several times over the years voiced a skeptical opinion about [Linux as a gaming platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_as_a_gaming_platform "Linux as a gaming platform").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-58) In 2013, he argued for [emulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emulation_(computing) "Emulation (computing)") as the "proper technical direction for gaming on Linux",[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-59) and in 2014 he voiced the opinion that Linux might be the biggest problem for the success of the [Steam Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_Machines "Steam Machines").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-60)

Carmack contributes to charities and gaming communities. Some of the recipients of Carmack's [charitable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charitable_organization "Charitable organization") contributions include his former high school, promoters of open-source software, opponents of software patents, and game enthusiasts.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-61)

## Personal life

Carmack was so successful at id that by mid-1994 he had purchased two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferraris "Ferraris"): a [Ferrari 328](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_328 "Ferrari 328") and a [Ferrari Testarossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_Testarossa "Ferrari Testarossa").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-lombardi199407-62) In 1997, he gave away the Ferrari 328 as a prize to [Dennis Fong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Fong "Dennis Fong"), the winner of the _Quake_ tournament "[Red Annihilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Annihilation "Red Annihilation")".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-63)

He met his now ex-wife [Katherine Anna Kang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Anna_Kang "Katherine Anna Kang") at the 1997 [QuakeCon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuakeCon "QuakeCon") when she visited id's offices. As a bet, Kang challenged Carmack to sponsor the first all-female _Quake_ tournament if she was able to produce a significant number of participants. Carmack predicted a maximum of 25 participants, but there were 1,500.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKushner2003281-64) Carmack and Kang married on January 1, 2000, and planned a ceremony in Hawaii. Steve Jobs requested that they would postpone the ceremony so Carmack could attend the MacWorld Expo on January 5, 2000. Carmack declined and suggested making a video instead.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-65) Carmack and Kang had a son Christopher Ryan in August 2004.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-66) Their second son was born in November 2009.

Carmack is divorced as of 2021. On May 26, 2022, he announced his divorce and how he met his partner Trista through the VR _[Beat Saber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat\_Saber "Beat Saber")_ games he would host via Twitter.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-67)

As a game developer, Carmack differed from many of his contemporaries by avoiding commitment to a final release date for any game he was developing. Instead, when asked for a release date on a new game, Carmack would usually reply that the game would be released "when it's done".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-68) Employees at [Apogee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_Realms "3D Realms"), in their past years the publishers of games by id Software, adopted this business practice as well.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-69) In 2019, as a guest on _[The Joe Rogan Experience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Joe\_Rogan\_Experience "The Joe Rogan Experience")_, Carmack stated that his beliefs have changed over time: "I largely recant from that now." On _[Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage\_(video\_game) "Rage (video game)")_'s six-year development time he says: "I think we should have done whatever it would have taken to ship that two years earlier." Carmack also reflected on the internal development of Quake in this regard and described it as "traumatic" and says id Software could have split the game into two parts and shipped it earlier.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-70)

Carmack has a [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog "Blog") last updated in 2006 (previously a [.plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger_protocol "Finger protocol") on id Software's server, under the username `johnc`[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-71)), an active [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account, and also occasionally posts comments to _[Slashdot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slashdot "Slashdot")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-slashdot-answers-10)

Carmack supported the [2012 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul_2012_presidential_campaign "Ron Paul 2012 presidential campaign") of [Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)")[Ron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul "Ron Paul"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-72) and also persuaded the [Libertarian Party of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_of_Texas "Libertarian Party of Texas") to accept [bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin "Bitcoin") as an alternative to donations.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-73) He is an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheism "Atheism").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-75) During a conversation with [Joe Rogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Rogan "Joe Rogan"), Carmack revealed that he had trained in Brazilian Jiu Jitsu and [Judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") for several years as a hobby.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-76)

During his time at id Software, a medium pepperoni pizza would arrive for Carmack from [Domino's Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domino's_Pizza "Domino's Pizza") almost every day,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-77) carried by the same delivery person for more than 15 years. Carmack had been such a regular customer that they continued to charge him 1995 prices.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-78)

On occasion he has commended the efforts of similarly focused programmers– first [Ken Silverman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Silverman "Ken Silverman"), who wrote the [Build engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build_(game_engine) "Build (game engine)") for [3D Realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_Realms "3D Realms"), and later with [Tim Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Sweeney_(game_developer) "Tim Sweeney (game developer)") of [Epic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Games "Epic Games"), who wrote the [Unreal Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Engine "Unreal Engine").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carmack#cite_note-slashdot-answers-10)
